content: I'm pretty new to using AI, and I was wondering if someone might be able to point me to instructions for how to use Lean 4 in the Claude web? I asked it to install it in its sandbox, and it said it did, but is there a more canonical approach? I don't trust Claude enough to want to have it installed locally or give it any of my credentials. I just want to let it check that the Lean code that it comes up with type checks so that it can recurse on it.
This isn't Claude code, just the Claude chat (I'm not sure what to call it).

From Claude:
How I got it working: elan's normal install failed because it fetches from release.lean-lang.org, which isn't on the allowlist. I downloaded the toolchain tarball directly from GitHub releases instead, installed zstd from apt to unpack it, and put the result in /home/claude/lean-tc. To use it in a later session I'd need to repeat that, which takes a few minutes, since the sandbox resets between tasks.
..
No Mathlib. Its cache host isn't reachable.
So I guess my question is, is there a more canonical approach to that, and can I get mathlib into it somehow?
I want to see if I can vibe code a systems programming language that is formally proved and that is easy to reason about so that the programs written in it are "easy" to prove correct.
